thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: canary group 'east-1a-v2' reporting node evictions and OOM kills after the 21:12 deploy. 502 spike ~00:30 - 02:00 window, error budget touched for canary. Metrics: eviction_rate=8.7%, 5xx_rate_canary=3.9%. Paging on-call: @jamal

jamal (on-call): I'm on it. pinging logs and trying to pull the pod / container traces. Anyone on release for this deploy?

alex (release): That was the lightweight routing change (commit 0f4a9d1). It toggled the prefix cache behavior. I flagged the change but didn’t expect memory pressure at this scale.

maria (sre): I'm seeing nodes in that canary hitting >92% RSS right before eviction. Heap growth ~linear with request rate. Could be unbounded cache growth in the new path.

linus (engineer): confirming. stack traces show repeated cache insertions from `router::prefix_cache::insert`, no eviction TTL applied. Patch was supposed to be safe.

jamal (on-call): Options: 1) flip the feature flag to disable new routing 2) revert the single commit 0f4a9d1 3) push a small hotfix that caps cache size. Which is fastest?

alex (release): Feature flag name is `ff:new_prefix_cache`. Flip it now and we can observe. I can do a kill-switch rollout from console.

release-bot: Actionable: feature flag `ff:new_prefix_cache` currently at 100% for east-1a-v2. To disable run: `rbctl feature disable ff:new_prefix_cache --env=canary --group=east-1a-v2`

maria (sre): Do it, please. If the flag is server-side we should be able to flip with zero deploy. If it's compiled in, revert is the fallback.

alex (release): running disable now...

alex (release): done. release-bot: executed `rbctl feature disable ff:new_prefix_cache --env=canary --group=east-1a-v2` :white_check_mark:

qa-bot: Note: after flag flip, synthetic traffic shows reduced memory footprint in 30s window.

maria (sre): Hmm metrics improved but a subset of pods still evicting. Looking at pod metadata — two nodes still on older agent kernel (node drift). They haven't picked up the flag change due to stale env cache on those machines.

linus (engineer): If it's env cache drift, we need either a restart of the process on those hosts or revert commit. Restarting pods in canary group is quick; I'll push rolling restart to the 4 affected pods. Command: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/router-canary -n inference --field-selector=spec.nodeName in (ip-10-0-1-23,ip-10-0-1-24)`

jamal (on-call): Do restart. Keep one pod up while others cycle to keep telemetry.

linus (engineer): restarting pods now... logs: restarting pod router-canary-5, router-canary-6...

maria (sre): Pods restarted. Early signs: eviction_rate dropping to 0.6% in canary; 5xx down to 0.3%.

alex (release): Good. Do we still need to revert commit 0f4a9d1 or can we ship a proper fix in the next patch? We should avoid full revert if the flag kill is sufficient.

jamal (on-call): Let's keep observation window 15m. If stable, we won't revert. But we need a customer impact assessment and postdeploy hotfix plan.

maria (sre): From the monitoring dashboard: user-facing latency increased ~120ms median and 4% of requests had 5xx during the 7 minute window between 21:14–21:21. Affected customers mostly API tier B and a handful of mid-market customers routing through east-1a. No data loss.

alex (release): I'll open an incident ticket and tag account-succcess for outreach. Incident severity provisional: Sev3 given limited customer impact but potential regressions.

jamal (on-call): Agree Sev3. Creating ticket IN-4521 with timeline and metrics.

linus (engineer): Also drafted a one-line rollback PR in case the flag flip + restart shows regression later: `git revert --no-edit 0f4a9d1 && ./deploy.sh --canary east-1a-v2`

alex (release): Keep that PR on standby but don't merge unless we see new evictions. We should schedule a hotfix that caps cache size: proposed minimal fix in router: `cache.max_entries = 10000` behind the flag.

maria (sre): Observability note: enable `prefix_cache.evictions` counter and a cpu/mem anomaly alert for canaries.

qa-bot: Canary synthetic checks stable for 10m. No new 5xx.

jamal (on-call): Observation window completed. Metrics are stable for 18m. I'm going to hand off to @elaine for overnight on-call with status. Elaine — summary: 21:12 deploy triggered cache growth in new routing path, flag kill + pod restart mitigated, latency/5xx spike for ~7 min, no ongoing impact.

elaine (on-call-next): Thanks, jamal. Taking handoff. I'll keep an eye for another 30m and then drop to standard on-call rotations.

alex (release): Follow-up actions: 1) linus to open hotfix PR to cap cache and add TTL 2) maria to add anomaly alerts and update runbook with env cache drift steps 3) release to add automated post-deploy check for env cache version consistency. Assigning owners.

linus (engineer): Opening PR now: https://git.redwood/s/repo/pulls/4522 — implements max_entries + TTL and unit tests.

maria (sre): Created alert rule AR-907 and added step to runbook: `if flag flip doesn't restore behavior within 2m -> restart canary pods in group; if still failing -> revert commit`

alex (release): Customer comms: draft message to affected customers noting increased latency and transient errors, mitigation steps taken, and offer to follow up. I'll cc account success.

jamal (on-call): Marking thread resolved for active incident: canary stabilized. Moving to postmortem channel later. Reacts: :thumbsup: from release, :eyes: from SRE.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: IN-4521 status changed to mitigated by jamal (on-call). Tags: canary, postdeploy, feature-flag, hotpatch

elaine (on-call-next): Taking over monitoring. If I see new evictions, I will escalate and run the rollback PR as last resort.

linus (engineer): Note to self: add detailed allocation logging to prefix_cache for easier root-cause follow-up.

alex (release): Thanks everyone. We'll schedule the hotfix to prod next patch window with QA signoff. Closing incident channel thread.
